Provide small prompt set and suggested perf test harness
action_items: Aria - send pricing + pilot template by 2026-12-08
Simon - attach console tour video and Optimize playbook snippets by 2026-12-09

header: Date: 2026-12-07 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m\nAttendees: Aria Gomez (Redwood AE), Simon Patel (Redwood SE), Rosa Liu (Redwood Product), Jared Mills (Catalyst Eng Mgr), Priya Rao (Catalyst ML Eng), Tomas Vega (Catalyst Infra)
summary: Introductory hosted API demo focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming behavior, key request params, and retry/backoff patterns. Walked Catalyst Retail through Console cost view and Optimize suggestions. Covered security questions (SOC2, KMS, VPC options) and agreed on a pilot and benchmark window.
topics: Hosted chat streaming, streaming heartbeat and SSE, token costs and truncation, concurrency and batching tradeoffs, retry/backoff patterns, idempotency for generation calls, console observability (per-route latency/cost), Optimize recommendations (prefix caching, quantization recommendations), security (KMS, SSO), pilot next steps
transcript:
00:00 Speaker 1: okay starting in just a second, um hi everyone this is Aria from Redwood, thanks for joining.
00:06 Jared Mills: hey thanks Aria, can you hear us? we're on west coast.
00:09 Speaker 1 (Aria): loud and clear. we've got about 40 minutes, we'll demo the hosted chat gen path, show console cost views and then go through retry/playbook patterns. Simon will do a quick deep dive too.
00:21 Tomas Vega: quick ask, are we expecting any slides or just live demo?
00:24 Aria Gomez: mix of both - one quick deck at top, then live Console and API sandbox.
00:30 Simon Patel: great, I'll start by showing a simple chat flow - three-turn convo - and then toggle streaming on so you can see partial tokens in the client.
00:38 Priya Rao: streaming is important for our product, we need sub-200ms first-byte ideally for chat UX, is that realistic on hosted?
00:45 Simon Patel: so for first-byte p95 we target 100-300ms depending on model size and seq-length; smaller models faster. one knob is to use the low-latency model variant and limit response length with max_tokens. also streaming onset depends on batching at high throughput.
00:59 Jared Mills: batching hurts our latency, we can't accept large batching windows. can you show how Redwood handles small batches?
01:06 Simon Patel: yes - continuous batching is workload-aware; we have a small-window mode that favors low latency, and an optimize recommendation in the Console that suggests batch size based on observed traffic. I'll flip that on.
01:20 Speaker 2 (Rosa): also worth noting we do prefix/KV caching - for repeated prompts it can shave tokens and time.
01:28 Priya Rao: nice. on retries — if we stream and connection drops mid-response, what's recommended pattern?
01:33 Simon Patel: good question. for streaming we recommend client-side reconnection with idempotency tokens — do a short-range resume when possible. our streaming protocol sends chunk offsets; if you get a transient transport failure, reconnect and request resume. for full request failures, we suggest exponential backoff with jitter and switch to a smaller model variant as fallback.
01:50 Tomas Vega: resume offsets sounds good; do we need to store server-side state?
01:54 Simon Patel: server keeps ephemeral KV cache for active sessions; resume refers to the token cursor in the generated stream. nothing persistent beyond the request window.
02:02 Jared Mills: security, couple items: we need SSO + SCIM provisioning, and customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. can Redwood hosted do customer KMS?
02:12 Aria Gomez: yes, we support enterprise KMS integrations (bring-your-own) and SAML SSO + SCIM. we'll share the integration notes. for the hosted plan there are controls for log redaction and audit logs.
02:23 Priya Rao: is there an option to run in VPC or is that only for the Private thing?
02:28 Aria Gomez: VPC peering/private deployment is in Private or Dedicated tiers; hosted offers fine-grained privacy controls and optional data retention toggles but if you need network-isolated deployments we'd move to Private.
02:40 Simon Patel: switching to the Console now. showing per-route latency, token breakdown, and cost by model. Priya, you can see how a single chat route's per-token cost spikes when max_tokens is high.
02:55 Priya Rao: how is cost calculated? tokenization differs across models - do you normalize?
03:01 Simon Patel: cost is normalized to a unit we call token-units, adjusted per model's sampling. Console shows both raw tokens and normalized cost. we can export CSV for your finance team.
03:12 Jared Mills: what's the easiest path to proof-of-value? we want a pilot that runs some real traffic.
03:16 Aria Gomez: two-week pilot produced by Redwood SE: we'll reserve a small hosted quota, run your prompt set, and capture p95 latency and cost. Simon can run parallel benches with our sandbox harness.
03:26 Tomas Vega: do you support load tests that emulate our bursty traffic?
03:30 Simon Patel: yes, we'll provide a harness and recommendations. also Console has a load-sim feature for model routing behavior.
03:38 Speaker 3 (Jared): can we see the API call shape? like headers, idempotency, streaming SSE?
03:43 Simon Patel: absolutely. here's cURL and a JavaScript example. I'll paste them into chat.
03:48 Simon Patel: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/generate 
03:52 Simon Patel: -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY' 
03:54 Simon Patel: -d '{"model":"rwd-small-chat-v1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What are our best sellers this quarter?"}],"stream":true,"idempotency_key":"<uuid>","max_tokens":150,"temperature":0.2}'
04:05 Priya Rao: about idempotency_key, does Redwood dedupe server-side or do you just use it for replay protection?
04:11 Simon Patel: we dedupe for a short window (60s by default) and tie it to request signatures. it's mainly to prevent double-charges and repeated generations; for longer dedupe windows you'd use your job queue semantics.
04:20 Jared Mills: mitigations for token inflation — any recommend truncation strategies?
04:24 Rosa Liu: yes, we often recommend prefix engineering and dynamic max_tokens based on the input length. Console Optimize suggests a max_tokens per route based on your observed reply length distribution. it also recommends caching common prompts.
04:35 Priya Rao: can Optimize recommend quantization or model switching? we have cost targets per 1k calls.
04:41 Simon Patel: Optimize will recommend either a smaller quantized variant or low-cost variant for bulk throughput routes. we'll show a cost-per-1k table in the export.
04:50 Tomas Vega: show me a failure scenario: high latency at peak, what's the fallback?
04:55 Simon Patel: we demo policy-based routing: route to low-latency model, if that fails fallback to cheaper variant or degrade to a short summary-only response. you can configure canary rollouts and automatic fallback in the Console.
05:10 Jared Mills: do you have SLO guarantees on hosted?
05:13 Aria Gomez: hosted is best-effort with published performance profiles; for contractual SLOs we do Dedicated with SLA. hosted customers often start on hosted and then move to Dedicated for production guarantees.
05:25 Priya Rao: show me a runtime trace for a single chat — how do we debug token-by-token latency?
05:30 Simon Patel: Console trace shows per-token micro-timings, kernel selection, and whether a cache hit occurred. watching a sample now - you can see first token at 120ms, then steady token generation.
05:46 Jared Mills: any gotchas around client-side timeouts? we don't want partial transcripts to be misinterpreted as final answers.
05:52 Simon Patel: set client-side timeouts longer than expected generation time for the max_tokens you allow. we also provide 'final' messages in the stream that explicitly mark end-of-response — handle those to avoid treating partial content as final.
06:08 Priya Rao: what about rate limiting — do you have a 429 pattern?
06:12 Aria Gomez: yes, we return standard 429 with Retry-After; for streaming we may send a separate control frame. backoff recommendations: exponential with full jitter starting at 200ms.
06:23 Tomas Vega: will 429s happen during pilot? we need predictable behavior for our integration tests.
06:28 Aria Gomez: for pilot we'll provision quota to avoid 429s for your expected load. if you plan large burst tests, we'll pre-coordinate.
06:34 Simon Patel: demo time — I'm going to run a live gen with stream=true; watch the partials.
06:38 Simon Patel: 06:38 [stream start] 06:40 Speaker 2 (Simon): okay chunk1: "Top sellers this quarter are" 06:44 chunk2: "— our limited-run jackets, the new summer sandal, and subscription boxes" 06:52 chunk3: "Est. revenue share: 28%, 14%, 11% respectively" 06:58 [stream end - final token sent]
07:02 Priya Rao: nice. what if the connection drops at chunk2?
07:06 Simon Patel: reconnect, request resume with idempotency_key and offset. if resume not supported (older client) restart request but use dedupe to avoid double-billing.
07:16 Rosa Liu: also you can checkpoint partials to S3 for long-running responses if you need persistence.
07:23 Jared Mills: question on tokenization: are embeddings and generation tokens billed separately?
07:27 Aria Gomez: yes we have separate pricing lines; we'll send an example billing sheet.
07:31 Tomas Vega: curious about logs - will PII ever be included in our logs?
07:35 Aria Gomez: we redact by default and offer redact-level controls; enterprise customers can opt to never persist logs or to send them to their own log sink.
07:44 Priya Rao: okay can we talk about integration complexity — what does a minimal integration look like?
07:49 Simon Patel: minimal is API key to backend service, call chat generate streaming, handle SSE events, and render partials. client libs exist for Node/Python. we also provide a sample front-end snippet for React.
08:00 Jared Mills: show us the SDK snippet for reconnect and resume.
08:04 Simon Patel: paste: js example with EventSource polyfill, reconnect logic with exponential backoff and resume offset handling.
08:18 Priya Rao: on the console Optimize tab, do you show suggested batching thresholds?
08:22 Simon Patel: yes Optimize proposes batch size, prefix cache rules, and model_quant recommendations. you can apply recommendations as one-click changes to route configs.
08:34 Tomas Vega: can we lock model versions for auditability? we need repeatability for A/B tests.
08:38 Rosa Liu: yes model pinning is supported per-route; you can pin exact version hashes and create release notes in Console.
08:46 Jared Mills: anything about safety filters and content moderation? we need auto-moderation for user content.
08:50 Aria Gomez: we include built-in safety filters and a moderation endpoint; you can also bring your own classifier to run pre- or post-generation.
08:59 Priya Rao: latency vs cost tradeoff example please — show numbers.
09:03 Simon Patel: for a 10-token response, small low-latency model might be $0.0008 per request with p95 120ms. quantized cheaper model might be $0.0004 with p95 220ms. I'll attach the detailed table post-call.
09:20 Jared Mills: we have PCI concerns in checkout flows — any references for compliance?
09:25 Aria Gomez: we'll send SOC2 + compliance pack; for PCI you should use Private or Dedicated with network isolation typically.
09:35 Priya Rao: what's the onboarding timeline? we want production in Q1.
09:38 Aria Gomez: typical path: pilot 2 weeks, iterate and instrument 2-4 weeks, then either scale on hosted or commit to Dedicated for SLOs — fits your Q1 target.
09:48 Simon Patel: let's demonstrate an error pattern: I'm forcing a timeout on the backend to show the client's retry behavior.
09:52 [demo glitch simulated] 09:55 Simon Patel: server returns 500 mid-stream. client reconnects, receives Retry-After, and we show the resume.
09:59 Priya Rao: in our app we want to show a spinner until final; should we hide partials?
10:03 Simon Patel: we recommend rendering partials for responsiveness but mark them as unstable until final message is received. also provide a cancel button to stop streaming.
10:12 Tomas Vega: question about observability APIs — can we pull per-request traces programmatically?
10:17 Rosa Liu: yes we expose REST endpoints to fetch traces and logs and you can route them to your S3 or Splunk.
10:24 Jared Mills: show me how Console correlates cost to routes.
10:28 Simon Patel: here — route view shows tokens per-request, model used, and cost. you can group by project/team tag.
10:36 Priya Rao: okay let's talk SLA triggers: when do we move to Dedicated?
10:40 Aria Gomez: when you need hard SLOs and capacity isolation; also required for on-prem or air-gapped. we can start conversations around capacity planning now.
10:49 Tomas Vega: last question - are there any known issues with WebSocket clients vs SSE?
10:53 Simon Patel: SSE is our recommended streaming surface; WebSockets supported but requires extra keepalive handling. SSE is simpler for browser-based flows.
11:03 Jared Mills: that covers most of it. can you recap next steps?
11:07 Aria Gomez: recap: Aria sends pricing and SOC2 docs; Simon sends console snippets, replay harness, and bench plan; Catalyst provides prompt set and target latency. we'll schedule pilot kickoff next week.
11:20 Priya Rao: thanks everyone.
11:22 Aria Gomez: thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invite and notes.
11:26 [call ends]
